title: Introduce CI-watcher, decompose build profiles, and lockfile prune
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have grown noisy and slow for mid-size changes. Two recurring sources are (1) full-matrix builds triggered by innocuous frontend/build profile tweaks and (2) stale deps causing intermittent cache misses and flaky lint runs. This PR introduces a small daemon (ci-watcher) plus repo layout changes to: 1) detect "partial-run" eligibility and only run the subset of CI jobs required; 2) decompose monolithic build profiles into per-target profiles so caches are more targeted; 3) add an automated lockfile-prune to remove unused transitive entries and surface version drift.

Design summary:
- ci-watcher: lightweight Go process that runs in the Actions preflight step. It inspects the git diff (paths + lockfile checksum) and consults .ci/partial-rules.yaml heuristics to decide which job groups to wake up. It emits a JSON manifest (.ci/ci-manifest.json) that downstream jobs use to skip or run.
- Build profiles: move build profiles from a single build/config.yaml to build/profiles/{service,frontend,examples}.yaml. Profiles are smaller, importable, and allow per-profile cache keys.
- Cache warming: add .ci/cache-warm.json to seed the bake stage for common artifacts identified in nightly telemetry.
- Lockfile prune: scripts/lockfile_prune.py examines yarn/pip/poetry lockfiles, removes entries not referenced by any package and writes a compact.lock with a deterministic header. It also produces a small audit report to be reviewed in PR body.

Rollout plan:
- Step 1 (this PR): add ci-watcher and decomposed profiles behind a feature flag (GH Action input ci_watcher=true by default for main).
- Step 2: run lockfile-prune in dry-run mode for a week to collect audit reports.
- Step 3: enable partial-run by default; monitor premerge latency and flake rate.

Backout plan:
- Revert GH workflow input to disable ci_watcher and revert to legacy build/config.yaml.
- Scripts are idempotent; pruning only writes compact.lock when run with --apply.

Checklist:
- [x] Add ci-watcher binary + Action wrapper
- [x] Introduce build/profiles layout and migration mapper
- [x] Add cache-warm manifest and update bake job
- [x] Add lockfile_prune script and dry-run audit mode
- [x] Update docs with upgrade guide and runbook
- [x] Add unit tests for partial-run heuristics
- [x] Smoke-tested against redwood/quickstarts and redwood-sdk-python

What changed (high-level):
- New GH workflow: .github/workflows/ci-watcher.yml
- New tool: tools/ci-watcher/main.go + internal heuristics
- Build profile decomposition: build/profiles/*
- Lockfile tool: scripts/lockfile_prune.py + tests/
- Cache warm manifest: .ci/cache-warm.json
- Docs: docs/ci/upgrade-guide.md and docs/ci/partial-run.md

How this helps:
- Median presubmit feedback time reduced by ~35% for changes touching a single package in experiments.
- Reduced wasted CI minutes for docs/examples-only PRs by avoiding JS build shards.
- Lockfile prune highlights hidden transitive drift and reduces install size in reproducible builds.

Limitations & notes:
- Partial-run heuristics are conservative; some cross-package changes still trigger full runs.
- We keep a feature flag to make rollback straightforward.
- The lockfile-prune behavior varies by package manager; for yarn/pnpm/poetry we added lightweight adapters.
